item.title: TAI #229: Fable 5.2 and the Case for a 2027 AI Takeoff
item.guid: title:tai 229 fable 5 2 and the case for a 2027 ai takeoff
item.description: Also, Gemini 4 Carbon puts Google back in the coding race, plus METR’s study of Anthropic, the AI 2027 forecast update, and Jensen Huang’s departure from NVIDIA. What happened this week in AI by Louie In August, AI researcher Romeo Dean put his median date for AI capable of doing virtually all white-collar work in early 2035. Last week, he moved it to September 2028. He is one of several leading AI researchers who have brought their timelines forward, and I am hearing a similar shift in my conversations with people at large companies about how much of the economy AI will change and how soon. I think there is a real chance that, one way or another, the world will look quite different two years from now. My own view started to change with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: Engineering AI Discover
item.guid: title:engineering ai discover
item.description: The challenges and decisions behind AI Discover’s intelligence layer By Varun Khaitan , Peng Ren , Gary Tang , Itay Teller , Atif Faheem , Nipun Kumar , Donnie DeBoer , Eduardo Lundgren , Matteo Rinaldi , Raghav Bakshi We recently introduced AI Discover , a new tab in our TV app where a small group of members can try new ways to find something to watch. For years, our recommendations have worked in the background, inferring what a member might enjoy from their viewing history. AI Discover moves from that silent ranking toward steerable discovery. A member picks a theme, say “Quick Watches,” and gets a row of matching titles, a short note on why they fit and a few narrower themes to try next. From there, they can keep narrowing, head somewhere new or tune what they see. Building AI Discover raised a question many teams will recognize: how do you deliver a better member experience with generative AI on TV without sacrificing speed, reliability or safety?
